claims: Most workers also pay the 2% Medicare levy
whys: The 2% is typed into the text instead of using MEDICARE_PCT (MEDICARE_LEVY.rate), so it will go stale if the rate changes. 'Most workers' is also a population claim with no source.

claims: LITO and the Medicare levy are identical in both years, so the saving is unaffected
whys: The Medicare levy low-income thresholds are indexed every year, so the Medicare levy is not necessarily identical in 2025-26 and 2026-27 at low incomes. Check the constants for both years.

claims: Returns lodged between July and October 2026 cover FY2025-26, which used the old 16% rate — income tax on $80,000 was ...; the deductions most people forget to claim
whys: This is time-bound copy that goes stale after 31 Oct 2026 (agent-lodged returns run later). The locked segment contains an em dash I could not change. 'Most people forget' is a population claim with no source.
constants: lodgement-season dates (SITE_CONFIG or a constants file)

claims: Your employer's 12% SG contribution on top of salary
whys: The rate is typed in by hand instead of using SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate, so it can drift from the engine.

claims: Medicare Levy Surcharge of 1–1.5% applies above ...; working holiday makers have their own 15% schedule (line 315)
whys: The MLS tier rates and the WHM rate are typed in by hand. The comment at line 173 says no WHM constant exists. They should come from MEDICARE_LEVY.surcharge tiers and a WHM constant.
constants: MEDICARE_LEVY.surcharge tier rates; new WHM constant

claims: The free area and tapers index on 1 July and did not change on 20 September 2026.
whys: Taper rates (50c, 60c, 40c) are fixed percentages and cannot index. The $150 and $256 allowance thresholds also appear to have stayed the same for several years, so it is not clear they index on 1 July at all. The same claim is in the code comments at line 49 of this file and lines 266 and 537 of the constants file.
The $53, $256 and $150 in the methodology formula are typed in, not taken from the constants (the same drift risk as the FAQ).
